title: Most people read that verse and keep walking.
paragraphs: Most people read that verse and keep walking.

Abraham planted a tree.
In the desert.
That is not a throwaway detail.
“Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.” — Genesis 21:33
Pause there.

A tree takes time.
Years.
Maybe decades.
So why would an old man, living as a stranger in the land, plant something he may never sit under for long?

Because Abraham was doing more than gardening.
He was preaching with his shovel.

He had just come through conflict.
Wells were disputed.
Promises still looked fragile.
Nothing about his life felt fully settled yet.
And still he planted.

That tree was a declaration:
“God will keep His word here.”
“My future is not built on what I can control.”
“This ground belongs to the God who outlives me.”
And that’s the detail many miss.

Abraham called on “the Everlasting God” while planting something that would outlast a season.
He was anchoring his temporary life to an eternal God.

That tree was worship.
That tree was faith.
That tree was a sermon in wood and roots.
But here’s what we miss even deeper:

We love instant proof.
God often asks for planted trust.

We want fruit by Friday.
God gives us promises big enough to outlive our panic.
And that points straight to Jesus.

At the cross, it looked like the promise was buried.
But three days later, resurrection broke through the dry ground of human hopelessness.
What looked delayed was never denied.
What looked dead was already under the power of the Everlasting God.

So when Abraham planted that tree, he was living the kind of faith every believer is called into:
not frantic striving,
but rooted trust.

Plant the prayer.
Plant the obedience.
Plant the repentance.
Plant the quiet faithfulness nobody claps for.
Because in Christ, nothing surrendered to God is wasted.

You may be in a dry season right now.
Still plant.
Still worship.
Still call on the name of the Lord.
The Everlasting God is not nervous about your future.
